statements.action_statement: Upgrade jinja2 to 3.1.6 or later. Until then, load models only from trusted publishers and review chat templates in the UI before use.
statements.status_notes: Chat and instruction templates are rendered in an ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment (modules/chat.py), and template content is loaded from model metadata (tokenizer.chat_template, modules/models_settings.py). A downloaded model can therefore supply attacker-controlled template content, which is the precondition for this sandbox breakout via the built-in |attr filter.

statements.impact_statement: Exploitation requires an application-defined custom filter that invokes a callable passed into it. The application registers no custom filters or globals on its Jinja environment (only from_string calls in modules/chat.py), so the indirect str.format path cannot be reached. Remediated anyway by the jinja2 3.1.6 upgrade.
Exploitation requires control of both template content and template filename. Templates are compiled with from_string, which takes no adversary-controlled filename.
The xmlattr filter injection affects HTML output. Rendered templates here become a text prompt sent to the model, not HTML returned to a browser, so the injected attributes have no sink.
Same analysis as CVE-2024-22195: rendered template output is a model prompt, not HTML.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade gradio to 4.31.4 or later. Interim: keep the default localhost binding, avoid --listen and --share, and require --gradio-auth wherever the UI is exposed.
statements.status_notes: The UI instantiates a gr.JSON component (modules/ui_chat.py), the component named in the local file inclusion advisory. Exposure depends on deployment: default binding is localhost, but --listen or --share makes the UI reachable by others.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade gradio to 5.0.0 or later. Interim: do not use --share.
statements.status_notes: Affects the public share tunnel, which the application exposes through its --share flag. Reachable only when a user enables sharing.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade gradio. Interim on Windows: localhost binding only and --gradio-auth if exposed.
statements.status_notes: Path traversal on Windows hosts. The project ships Windows launchers (cmd_windows.bat), so Windows deployments are in scope; Linux and macOS deployments are not.

statements.impact_statement: The advisory describes command injection in a repository CI workflow (test-functions), not in the published package. That code is not present in the installed wheel.
The ReDoS is in transformers.testing_utils, a test helper. The application never imports it (no references in the codebase).
Code injection in the SEW convert_config checkpoint-conversion utility. The application loads models through standard loaders and never invokes upstream conversion scripts.

statements.status_notes: The advisory concerns the Trainer class. The application's training tab instantiates transformers.Trainer (modules/training.py). Reachability depends on whether attacker-supplied checkpoints reach the vulnerable path; analysis open.

Path traversal in load_checkpoint_in_model. Model loading uses accelerate for device placement, so a malicious model repository may reach this path. Confirming whether the application's loader invokes the vulnerable function.
